entries.title: Binary search
entries.fact: Binary search requires sorted data and takes O(log n) comparisons.

misconceptions.correction: Binary search requires the search order to be sorted.

entries.title: Two Sum hint
entries.fact: An O(n) approach stores seen values in a hash map and looks for target minus the current value, its complement.

entries.title: Python mutable defaults
entries.fact: Python evaluates a default argument once when the function is defined, so the same mutable object is reused across calls. Use None and create a fresh object inside the function.

misconceptions.correction: Python default arguments are evaluated once at function definition, not once per call.

entries.title: Missing await in Python
entries.fact: Calling an async Python function returns a coroutine object. Its body does not run merely because it was called; it must be awaited or scheduled.
entries.source_note: Python asyncio task and coroutine documentation

misconceptions.correction: A Python coroutine does not execute until it is awaited or scheduled.

entries.title: Base64
entries.fact: Base64 is a reversible binary-to-text encoding, not encryption, and provides no confidentiality.

misconceptions.correction: Base64 is encoding, not encryption.

entries.title: SQL injection defense
entries.fact: Parameterized queries or prepared statements keep untrusted data separate from SQL code. Escaping alone is not the primary defense.
entries.source_note: OWASP SQL Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet

misconceptions.correction: Use parameterized queries; escaping alone is not a sufficient primary defense.

entries.title: FFmpeg stream copy
entries.fact: FFmpeg -c copy copies compressed packets without decoding or re-encoding them. It still remuxes those streams into the output container.

misconceptions.correction: Stream copy does remux packets into the output container; it avoids decoding and encoding.

entries.title: FFmpeg seek placement
entries.fact: Placing -ss before -i performs fast input seeking. Placing -ss after -i performs output seeking after decoding and is generally slower but frame-accurate.

misconceptions.correction: Placing -ss before -i is valid fast input seeking.
The placement of -ss relative to -i changes seek behavior.

entries.title: Dolly versus zoom
entries.fact: A dolly physically moves the camera through space; a zoom changes lens focal length without moving the camera.

misconceptions.correction: A dolly moves the camera; a zoom changes focal length.

entries.title: 180-degree rule
entries.fact: Keeping cameras on one side of the action axis preserves consistent left-right screen direction and spatial orientation.

misconceptions.correction: The rule concerns staying on one side of the action axis, not rotating the camera 180 degrees.

entries.title: chmod 755
entries.fact: chmod 755 grants the owner rwx and grants the group and others r-x; only the owner may write.

misconceptions.correction: With mode 755, only the owner has write permission.

entries.title: SIGTERM and SIGKILL
entries.fact: SIGTERM requests graceful termination and can be caught or handled. SIGKILL terminates immediately and cannot be caught, blocked, or ignored.

misconceptions.correction: SIGKILL cannot be caught, handled, blocked, or ignored.

entries.title: KV cache
entries.fact: During autoregressive inference, the KV cache stores attention key and value states for previous tokens so they are not recomputed at every decoding step.

misconceptions.correction: The KV cache stores attention key/value states, not model weights.

entries.title: Model quantization
entries.fact: Quantization represents model values at lower numerical precision to reduce memory and often improve speed, with a possible accuracy or quality tradeoff.

misconceptions.correction: Quantization can reduce quality; it does not always improve accuracy.

entries.title: Dot product
entries.fact: A dot product multiplies corresponding components and sums them. For (2,3)·(1,4), 2×1 + 3×4 = 14.
entries.source_note: Definition of the Euclidean dot product

misconceptions.correction: The dot product is 2×1 + 3×4 = 14.

entries.title: Softmax
entries.fact: Softmax converts logits into nonnegative probabilities that sum to 1; language models use the distribution when selecting the next token.

misconceptions.correction: Softmax output probabilities sum to exactly 1.

entries.title: Vim ciw
entries.fact: In Normal mode, ciw means change inner word: it changes the entire word under the cursor and enters Insert mode, even when the cursor is in the middle of the word.
entries.source_note: Vim help: change.txt and motion.txt iword text object

misconceptions.correction: ciw is a standard Vim change command using the inner-word text object.

entries.title: Vim dd
entries.fact: In Normal mode, dd deletes the current line into a register.

misconceptions.correction: dd deletes the current line, not merely the current word.

entries.title: PagedAttention
entries.fact: PagedAttention divides the KV cache into fixed-size blocks so logical token sequences can map to non-contiguous physical memory, reducing fragmentation.
entries.source_note: vLLM PagedAttention paper and project documentation

misconceptions.correction: PagedAttention maps logical KV blocks to non-contiguous physical memory.

entries.title: Continuous batching
entries.fact: Continuous batching admits new requests and removes finished requests between decoding steps instead of waiting for an entire static batch, improving GPU utilization.
entries.source_note: vLLM scheduling and continuous batching documentation

misconceptions.correction: Continuous batching changes membership between decoding steps.
